summary.text:
The user wants me to propose a general comparison method for evaluating two readings of unpointed Hebrew or Aramaic text. I need to return only a JSON object matching the specified schema.
{
  "written_text_status": "The unpointed consonantal text is primary and controlling; vocalizations are interpretive devices whose validity must be evaluated against the consonantal skeleton.",
  "admissibility_gate": "A candidate reading is admissible if it (1) reproduces the consonantal skeleton under standard orthographic conventions (2) yields grammatically coherent syntax and morphology in Hebrew or Aramaic  (3) can be lexically justified by attested roots or reasonably reconstructed forms attested elsewhere in the corpus.",
  "hard_disqualifiers": [
    "produces a string that cannot be reconciled with the consonantal text without ad-hoc emendation ",
    "violates core Hebrew/Aramaic morphosyntactic rules (e.g., impossible gender/number agreement, invalid root-and-pattern)",
    "requires a root or lexeme not attested in any Hebrew or Aramaic corpus",
    "produces a meaning that is semantically impossible in context"
  ],
  "comparison rules": [
    {
      "rule_id": "R1",
      "title": "Admissibility Gate",
      "operation": "HARD_CONSTRAINT",
      "rule": "Only readings that satisfy all admissibility criteria enter comparison; others are eliminated.",
      "justification": "Prevents comparison of unequal candidates; 'possible' is necessary but not sufficient."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R2",
      "title": "Immediate Context Primacy",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Prefer the reading that yields better semantic and syntactic coherence with the immediately surrounding clauses and discourse structure.",
      "justification": "Authors write for local intelligibility; local context is the strongest non-textual control."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R3",
      "title": "Grammar and Lexicon Naturalness",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Favor the reading whose morphology and lexical choice align with the most frequent and unmarked patterns in the language.",
      "justification": "Rare or forced constructions are less likely unless context demands them."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R4",
      "title": "Manuscript Support",
      "operation": "SOURCE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Weight readings by the number and independence of early Hebrew manuscripts that preserve them.",
      "justification": "Early Hebrew witnesses provide direct access to the consonantal text."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R5",
      "title": "Ancient Translations",
      "operation": "SOURCE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Weight translations by their fidelity to the Hebrew and their independence from one another.",
      "justification": "Translations reflect ancient interpretive traditions.

{
  "written_text_status": "The unpointed consonantal string is the fixed primary datum. Every candidate must be a phonologically and morphologically viable analysis of that string (within period-normal orthographic variation such as plene/defective spelling). Vocalization, morphological segmentation, and lexical assignment are interpretive hypotheses about the written text, not replacements for it.",
  "admissibility_gate": [
    "Exact match to the given consonants, allowing only standard orthographic variation attested for the period and corpus (matres lectionis conventions, common plene/defective alternation).",
    "Yields a morphologically well-formed word or phrase under descriptive Biblical Hebrew or Biblical Aramaic grammar.",
    "Corresponds to a lexeme (or transparent derivation) attested in Biblical Hebrew/Aramaic or closely related Northwest Semitic with a semantically usable range.",
    "Produces a clause that is syntactically parseable in the immediate context without requiring unattested constructions.",
    "Does not depend on emending the consonants or inventing an unattested root solely to rescue the reading."
  ],
  "hard_disqualifiers": [
    "Requires changing one or more consonants without independent manuscript support or a paleographically routine error type.",
    "Produces outright ungrammatical syntax or semantic nonsense that cannot be resolved by known BH/BA constructions.",
    "Rests on a completely unattested root or meaning lacking morphological, contextual, or comparative Semitic support.",
    "Creates an irreconcilable contradiction with unambiguous immediate context in the absence of other textual disruption signals.",
    "Double-counts the same stemma or treats a paraphrastic/secondary witness as if it were an independent Hebrew reading."
  ],
  "comparison_rules": [
    {
      "rule_id": "R1",
      "title": "Admissibility before comparison",
      "operation": "HARD_CONSTRAINT",
      "rule": "Apply the admissibility gate first. Only readings that pass every gate criterion enter comparative evaluation; failing readings are eliminated, not weighed.",
      "justification": "Ensures comparison occurs only among genuinely possible analyses of the same written text; possibility is necessary but not sufficient for preference."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R2",
      "title": "Immediate context and syntax primacy",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Prefer the reading that yields superior semantic fit, discourse coherence, and syntactic naturalness with the immediately surrounding clauses.",
      "justification": "Local intelligibility is the strongest internal control once consonants are fixed; authors write for readers who encounter the clause in sequence."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R3",
      "title": "Morphological and lexical naturalness",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Prefer the analysis that uses common morphology and well-attested senses over rare, forced, or hapax-dependent analyses unless context clearly requires the rarer option.",
      "justification": "Common forms and senses are the default expectation; rarity must be earned by contextual necessity, not assumed."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R4",
      "title": "Book-level and authorial usage",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "When a lexeme, construction, or formula shows clear preferences inside the same book or tightly related corpus, prefer the reading that aligns with those patterns.",
      "justification": "Internal consistency within a literary unit is stronger evidence than generic corpus frequency alone."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R5",
      "title": "Independent early Hebrew manuscript support",
      "operation": "SOURCE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Give strong positive weight to early Hebrew witnesses (especially DSS and other pre-medieval Hebrew manuscripts) that independently support one vocalization-compatible analysis or a relevant orthographic cue; do not equate medieval MT copies with independent confirmation.",
      "justification": "Early Hebrew manuscripts are direct witnesses to the written tradition closer to the compositional period."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R6",
      "title": "Ancient versions as indirect evidence",
      "operation": "SOURCE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Treat versions (LXX, Targums, Peshitta, Vulgate, etc.) as evidence of how ancient readers understood the consonants, weighted by demonstrated translation technique, independence, and degree of formal equivalence; never treat a version as equal to a Hebrew manuscript.",
      "justification": "Versions can preserve early interpretive traditions but are filtered through translation strategy and target language."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R7",
      "title": "Received pointing and accents",
      "operation": "SOURCE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Count Masoretic vocalization and accents as a strong early reading tradition that supplies a default analysis, but allow them to be outweighed by cumulative higher-tier internal and early manuscript evidence.",
      "justification": "The pointing is a carefully transmitted interpretive layer, not the consonants themselves; it deserves weight without automatic finality."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R8",
      "title": "Ketiv/Qere and known alternative traditions",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Treat Ketiv/Qere pairs and other ancient alternative notations as evidence that multiple analyses were already recognized; use them to support admissibility of alternatives, not as automatic victory for either side.",
      "justification": "They document historical awareness of ambiguity without by themselves deciding original intent."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R9",
      "title": "Canonical and formulaic parallels",
      "operation": "COMPARATIVE_WEIGHT",
      "rule": "Give supporting weight to clear parallel passages or fixed formulae only when the parallel is textually close and the shared language is diagnostic; do not force harmonization.",
      "justification": "Genuine parallels can disambiguate idiom; over-harmonization invents evidence."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R10",
      "title": "Symmetrical documentation and falsifiers",
      "operation": "REPORTING",
      "rule": "Score both readings on the same criteria in the same order; explicitly state what evidence would reverse the preference for each reading.",
      "justification": "Symmetry and falsifiability prevent one-sided special pleading."
    },
    {
      "rule_id": "R11",
      "title": "Underdetermination declaration",
      "operation": "TIE_BREAK",
      "rule": "If residual support remains roughly balanced after higher-tier criteria, declare the case underdetermined rather than forcing a winner.",
      "justification": "Honest underdetermination is preferable to manufactured certainty."
    }
  ],
  "evidence_hierarchy": [
    {
      "evidence": "Given unpointed consonants of the locus",
      "default_role": "CONTROLLING",
      "conditions": "All candidates must account for them; only routine orthographic variation is allowed."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Immediate syntactic and discourse context",
      "default_role": "STRONG",
      "conditions": "Always applied first among comparative factors; strongest internal discriminator."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Descriptive morphology and syntax of BH/BA",
      "default_role": "STRONG",
      "conditions": "Use standard descriptive grammars; prefer natural parses over strained ones."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Lexical attestation and sense distribution in BH/BA and closely related corpora",
      "default_role": "STRONG",
      "conditions": "Common senses preferred; rare senses require contextual necessity."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Book-level or authorial usage patterns",
      "default_role": "SUPPORTING",
      "conditions": "Applied when clear distributional preferences exist inside the same literary unit."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Independent early Hebrew manuscripts (e.g., DSS)",
      "default_role": "STRONG",
      "conditions": "Strong when they preserve relevant orthography or confirm one analysis; weight by independence and date."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Masoretic vocalization, accents, and standard MT tradition",
      "default_role": "STRONG",
      "conditions": "Default traditional analysis; rebuttable by cumulative higher-tier internal and early manuscript evidence."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Ketiv/Qere and other ancient alternative notations",
      "default_role": "SUPPORTING",
      "conditions": "Indicates historical plurality; supports admissibility more than final decision."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Ancient versions (LXX, Targums, Peshitta, Vulgate, etc.)",
      "default_role": "SUPPORTING",
      "conditions": "Weight by translation technique and independence; reduced force if paraphrastic or free."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Samaritan Pentateuch (Torah only)",
      "default_role": "CONTEXT_DEPENDENT",
      "conditions": "Useful early witness but adjust for known sectarian tendencies."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Canonical or formulaic parallels",
      "default_role": "SUPPORTING",
      "conditions": "Only when parallelism is close and diagnostic; no forced harmonization."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Medieval Jewish commentaries and modern scholarly opinion/consensus",
      "default_role": "EXCLUDED",
      "conditions": "May surface arguments already grounded in primary evidence; cannot supply independent weight or break ties."
    },
    {
      "evidence": "Denominational authority or popularity of an interpretation",
      "default_role": "EXCLUDED",
      "conditions": "Never used to prefer a reading."
    }
  ],
  "received_pointing_role": "REBUTTABLE_PRESUMPTION",
  "received_pointing_rule": "Masoretic vowels and accents function as a rebuttable presumption of the traditional reading of the consonants. They carry substantial weight as a carefully preserved early interpretive tradition, yet they may be set aside when immediate context, morphology/lexicon, and independent early Hebrew evidence cumulatively favor another admissible analysis. Accents are treated as interpretive punctuation, not as independent proof of morphology. Ketiv preserves the written form; Qere records a traditional reading and does not automatically override the consonants.",
  "burden_of_proof_rule": "Relative to the unpointed consonants, both admissible readings begin with equal formal standing. Evidential burden is comparative and effectively asymmetrical in application: the reading that better satisfies higher-tier criteria (immediate context, grammatical/lexical naturalness, independent early Hebrew support) prevails. A departure from the received Masoretic vocalization requires a clear positive advantage on those higher-tier grounds, not mere theoretical possibility. Absence of evidence is not evidence for novelty; the weaker or more ad-hoc reading bears the practical burden of justification.",
  "dependent_witness_rule": "Collapse genealogically dependent witnesses to a single stemma node before weighing. Multiple medieval MT manuscripts do not multiply the force of the received pointing. Version sub-traditions that share a common translation or revision event count once. DSS aligned with the Masoretic text-type are not independent of MT for pointing disputes; clearly independent DSS readings receive separate weight. Never double-count a version and a later witness derived from it.",
  "source_bias_rule": "Apply a uniform, pre-stated discount for known translational or ideological tendencies, regardless of which candidate benefits. Paraphrastic or theologically expansive sources (certain Targums, free LXX contexts) receive reduced force for fine-grained vocalization recovery; more formal-equivalence renderings receive higher force. Sectarian or revisionist witnesses are discounted precisely where a reading serves an identifiable agenda. The same bias adjustment must be applied symmetrically in every case.",
  "special_context_rules": [
    "Poetry: allow greater syntactic and lexical flexibility; use parallelism as a supporting disambiguator when clear.",
    "Proper names and technical/cultic terms: prioritize onomastic and extra-biblical attestation patterns.",
    "Legal or formulaic prose: prefer consistency with parallel legal formulations when genuinely parallel.",
    "Biblical Aramaic clauses: apply BA grammar and lexicon, not Hebrew defaults.",
    "Orthographic rarity: a reading that requires unusual spelling needs period-appropriate parallels.",
    "Suspected textual corruption: only invoke after admissible unemended readings fail; prefer the least invasive explanation."
  ],
  "tie_rule": "If, after ordered application of hard constraints and higher-tier comparative criteria, the two readings remain roughly balanced, declare the case underdetermined and report both as viable. Do not manufacture a preference. The received pointing may be noted as the traditional reading without being declared original. Prefer the reading that requires fewer ad-hoc assumptions only when that difference is itself clear and pre-specified; otherwise leave the tie unbroken.",
  "anti_ad_hoc_safeguards": [
    "Freeze the full hierarchy, weights, and special-context categories before inspecting the specific disputed form.",
    "Prohibit introduction of new criteria or re-weighting after observing which reading they favor.",
    "Require symmetrical scoring tables for both readings on the same ordered criteria.",
    "Any claimed exception must fall under a pre-declared special-context category and be applied consistently across cases.",
    "Ban appeals to unspecified scholarly consensus, denominational tradition, or 'the obvious sense' that lack primary-text anchors.",
    "Require explicit statement of falsifying evidence for whatever reading is preferred.",
    "Document the decision path so an independent evaluator can reproduce the same outcome from the same rules."
  ],
  "proposed_baseline": "Gate candidates strictly by consonantal fidelity, morphological possibility, lexical attestation, and local syntactic parseability. Among admissible readings, rank by ordered comparative force: (1) immediate contextual and syntactic coherence, (2) morphological and lexical naturalness within attested usage, (3) independent early Hebrew manuscript support, (4) book-level usage patterns, (5) ancient versions weighted by technique and independence, (6) received Masoretic pointing and accents as a strong but rebuttable traditional analysis. Collapse dependent witnesses, discount known biases symmetrically, and apply pre-declared special-context rules only. Prefer a reading only when it holds a clear cumulative advantage on higher-tier criteria; otherwise declare underdetermination. Exclude modern popularity, denominational authority, and post-hoc reweighting. The method is frozen prior to any specific disputed word.",
  "clarifications_needed": [
    "Exact operational thresholds for 'clear cumulative advantage' versus residual balance.",
    "Corpus-period definition of allowable orthographic variation for each major biblical section.",
    "How heavily a single high-quality independent DSS orthographic cue should weigh against a uniform MT pointing tradition.",
    "Handling of mixed Hebrew-Aramaic or heavily formulaic liturgical contexts."
  ],
  "confidence": "HIGH"
}
